brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: One Hex base, North half (piece:0,0,0;half-n) is the only base. Nothing was added beside or on top of it; the only other part is the drawer built into its cut face.

The configurator offers drawers only on the cut face of a half base, and a single cell offers one drawer position (socket s1, key 's'). A second key on the same cell is refused (HOST_MISMATCH). So one base holds one drawer, not five. Only one drawer was placed (drawer:0#0,0#cut).

finish.summary: I built a single hex base as a North half base with one drawer on its cut face, and nothing else added. The brief asked for five drawers in that base, but the configurator allows only one drawer per base cell, so five cannot be built in one base. Check_build reports the mesh as clear, with only an informational note that the open faces could take caps, which I left off because you asked for nothing else added. To get more drawers you would need more base cells, which goes beyond a single base.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
